title: Your Horoscope This Week: July 26 To August 1
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: July 26 To August 1

Cosmic beings, welcome to the final week of July, and it happens to be one of the most astrologically active weeks of the month. As the week begins, Saturn starts its retrograde in Aries, just days after Mercury ended its own retrograde. Saturn’s energy tends to be less in our faces because its lessons unfold slowly, through responsibility, discipline, and the work we know deep down still needs to be done. Between now and December, old promises we made to ourselves may come back into focus, along with unfinished projects, health goals, professional obligations, or personal commitments we’ve been procrastinating on because they felt too overwhelming. The best way to work with Saturn retrograde is to be painfully honest about what that work is, then break it down into actionable steps instead of letting it loom over you. The more accountable you become now, the more satisfying it will feel when Saturn shifts direct at the end of the year and you can clearly see what your consistency created.

That same day, July 26th, the lunar nodes change signs and begin a brand-new eighteen-month chapter. The North Node leaves Pisces and enters Aquarius, while the South Node leaves Virgo and enters Leo, shifting our collective destiny toward humanitarianism, innovation, community, and finding solutions that serve more than one person at a time. The South Node in Leo asks us to release the shadows of extreme independence, ego, selfishness, or believing we have to do everything alone to prove our strength. What makes this especially interesting is that we’re also in the first full week of Leo Season, with Jupiter newly in Leo, so we still benefit enormously from Leo’s courage, confidence, creativity, and willingness to be seen. The lesson is learning how to let our individual light shine while remembering that it takes a village to build the future we keep saying we want.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon brings this nodal shift fully into our emotional awareness and closes the month on a powerful note. This Full Moon connects us back to the intentions we set around the Aquarius New Moon and solar eclipse on February 17th, which also marked the beginning of the Year of the Fire Horse. Think back to where you were then, what you were hoping for, what you were ready to change, and how far that horse has already trotted over the past six months. This is a moment to celebrate what has manifested, acknowledge how much you’ve evolved, and recognize the people, communities, and unexpected opportunities that helped you get here. And if something you called in around February still feels unfinished, keep the faith. Eclipse season is right around the corner, and the first days of August may bring the movement or breakthrough you’ve been waiting for.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, Saturn retrograde begins in your sign this week, and it’s time to get serious about the goals you keep saying you’ll come back to. Over the next four and a half months, personal plans that were delayed, avoided, or left half-finished may demand more of your attention, along with the habits and mindsets that have quietly been slowing you down. You’re being asked to take greater responsibility for your growth without turning your life into one long productivity boot camp. Simplify your priorities, create a realistic game plan, and give yourself enough structure to stay consistent without burning out.

The North Node enters Aquarius this week and begins an eighteen-month journey through your friendship, community, and social network sector, encouraging you to become much more intentional about who you surround yourself with and how you show up online. Your connections can open major doors during this chapter, but quality matters more than collecting followers, invitations, or attention for the sake of feeling seen. With the South Node now in Leo, you’re also releasing the need to perform for validation and learning how to let your confidence speak for itself.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon brings something full circle in your friendship, technology, or social network sector. Think back to the fresh start you initiated around the Aquarius solar eclipse on February 17th, because a result, revelation, celebration, or important next step may emerge now. Pay attention to what is being illuminated about your community and your future. You’re entering a new chapter with a much clearer understanding of who belongs in it.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, Saturn retrograde begins in your spirituality and solitude sector this week, and the inner work you’ve been postponing may start asking for your attention. Old fears, buried emotions, and patterns you thought you had moved past could resurface over the next four and a half months, but healing doesn’t have to mean replaying every painful memory until you’re exhausted. You can heal through embodiment, movement, meditation, decluttering, better sleep, and creating enough quiet to hear yourself clearly. The actions you take in the present moment can release more than constantly analyzing the past.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your career sector, pushing you far beyond what feels familiar. This chapter is disruptive in the most necessary way, because your best opportunities will come from experimenting, taking risks, and doing things differently than you usually would. At the same time, the South Node enters Leo in your home and family sector, asking you to release unhealthy family programming, enabling patterns, or toxic dynamics that have been normalized for too long. Your outer life can only expand as much as your inner foundation is willing to change.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon brings a major wake-up call in your career sector. Something that began around the February 17th solar eclipse may now come full circle through a revelation, result, ending, or bold new direction. The past six months have been leading you here, and the Fire Horse energy is fully awake now, ready to gallop. Your job is to stop standing in its way.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, you just made it through your ruler Mercury’s retrograde, and now Saturn begins its retrograde in your friendship, technology, and social network sector. Over the next four and a half months, you may need to reassess the communities you’re part of, the role you play within them, and which long-term goals still deserve your energy. Some connections may require stronger boundaries, while others may reveal where more consistency and follow-through are needed. Be intentional about your online presence too, because Saturn wants your influence to have substance behind it.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your expansion sector, opening a major destiny chapter around travel, higher education, teaching, publishing, entrepreneurship, and seeing more of the world. Opportunities may come through returning to school, sharing what you know, or saying yes to experiences that stretch your perspective. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your communication sector, encouraging you to speak with greater purpose and release the habit of talking, posting, or performing simply to be seen.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates just how far you’ve come since the February 17th solar eclipse and the start of the Year of the Fire Horse. A vision you had around travel, education, business, or your larger life path may now feel much closer, or you may receive a clear sign about the next step. Six months later, the horse is still moving, and this Full Moon helps you recognize that you’ve covered more ground than you thought.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, you just made it through Mercury retrograde in your own sign, and now Saturn begins its retrograde in your transformation, merging, and outside-resources sector. This is a quieter, more subconscious transit, but it can be deeply excavating over the next four and a half months. You’re being asked to evaluate where your energy goes, how you handle shared money, and who you choose to merge with sexually, emotionally, and spiritually. Pay attention to the bonds that leave you feeling nourished versus the ones that quietly drain you.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your health, work, and routine sector, making your day-to-day well-being a major part of your destiny timeline. This is your cue to take your body, schedule, and energy management more seriously, even through small changes that are actually sustainable. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your money sector, revealing financial habits, spending patterns, or beliefs about security that are ready to evolve.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates what is and isn’t working within your routines, work style, health habits, and mindset. Something that began around the February 17th solar eclipse may now reach a turning point, showing you where progress has already been made and where a reset is overdue. Let the truth of your everyday life guide your next move, because the habits you repeat are shaping the future you keep asking for.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, Saturn retrograde begins in your expansion sector this week, asking you to get more serious about the future you keep envisioning. Over the next four and a half months, plans connected to travel, school, teaching, publishing, entrepreneurship, or a major leap of faith may need to be revisited and given more structure. Some dreams may have been delayed because the timing was off, while others need a stronger foundation before they can fully take off. This is your chance to refine the plan, handle the paperwork, strengthen your expertise, and make sure your next big move can actually support the life you want.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your partnership sector, making relationships, collaborations, and one-on-one connections a major part of your destiny timeline. At the same time, the South Node enters your sign, and you’re likely to feel this shift more personally than most. Over the next year and a half, you’ll be releasing outdated identities, attention-seeking patterns, and versions of yourself that were built around always having to be the strongest, brightest, or most impressive person in the room. You’re still meant to shine, especially with Jupiter in Leo, but this chapter teaches you how to share the stage, receive support, and let intimacy transform you.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your relationship sector and brings something full circle from the February 17th solar eclipse. A partnership may deepen, reach a turning point, or reveal exactly what your next step needs to be. Pay close attention to who is showing up for you now and how you feel when you’re around them. The new chapter ahead is less about doing everything alone and more about recognizing which connections are truly capable of growing with you.

Virgo Sun & Rising:

Virgo, Saturn retrograde begins in your intimacy, transformation, and shared-resources sector this week, asking you to take a closer look at what you owe, what you share, and where your energy has become too entangled. Over the next four and a half months, debts, taxes, investments, outside funding, or emotionally complicated bonds may need more attention than you’ve been giving them. This is also deeply psychological territory, so notice where fear, control, or difficulty trusting others has been shaping your choices. Handle what needs handling piece by piece rather than letting it grow into one giant monster under the bed.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your health, work, and routine sector, making the way you structure your everyday life central to your evolution. New technology, unconventional wellness practices, or a completely different work rhythm could help you become more efficient without running yourself into the ground. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your spirituality and subconscious sector, helping you release old fears, self-sabotaging habits, and the tendency to disappear into isolation whenever life feels overwhelming.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your routines, work life, and well-being, revealing what has genuinely improved since the February 17th solar eclipse and what still needs adjusting. A professional project, health goal, or lifestyle change may reach an important milestone, or your body may make it very clear where your current schedule is unsustainable. Let this Full Moon help you build a daily life that supports the future you’re calling in, because your habits are about to matter more than ever.

Libra Sun & Rising:

Libra, Saturn retrograde begins in your partnership sector this week, and the next four and a half months may require a more honest look at how you show up in your closest relationships. Commitments, boundaries, expectations, and unresolved dynamics could come back around, especially in connections where you’ve been doing too much, avoiding diﬃcult conversations, or hoping things would somehow sort themselves out. This is your chance to define what partnership actually means to you now and create relationships that feel more balanced, mature, and sustainable.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your fate, creativity, romance, and inner child sector, encouraging you to take your joy much more seriously. Love, art, pleasure, visibility, and passion projects can all become part of your destiny timeline, especially when you’re willing to experiment and follow what genuinely excites you. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your friendship and social network sector, helping you release group dynamics, online spaces, and connections that revolve around popularity, performance, or being liked by everyone.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your creative and romantic life, bringing something full circle from the February 17th solar eclipse. A love story, passion project, personal dream, or inner child healing journey may reach a major milestone, or you may finally understand what your heart has been trying to tell you for the past six months. Let yourself celebrate what has grown, and follow the spark that feels too alive to ignore.

Scorpio Sun & Rising:

Scorpio, Saturn retrograde begins in your health, work, and routine sector this week, asking you to take a more honest look at the systems holding your life together. Over the next four and a half months, unfinished work obligations, neglected health goals, or habits that have been draining your energy may come back into focus. You don’t need to overhaul your entire life in one dramatic sweep, but you do need a routine that supports the version of you you’re becoming. Simplify where you can, strengthen your boundaries around work, and stop treating rest like something you have to earn after reaching total exhaustion.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your home, family, and roots sector, making your private life a major part of your destiny timeline. A move, renovation, relocation, family shift, or deeper sense of emotional security could become increasingly important during this chapter. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your career and public image sector, helping you release the pressure to constantly prove yourself through titles, achievements, or how impressive your life appears from the outside. Success may start looking more like peace, stability, and having somewhere you can fully exhale.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your home and family sector, bringing something full circle from the February 17th solar eclipse. A living situation, family matter, emotional realization, or decision about where you belong may reach a turning point. The past six months have been showing you what kind of foundation your next chapter requires, and this Full Moon makes the answer much harder to ignore.

Sagittarius Sun & Rising:

Sag, Saturn retrograde begins in your creativity, romance, fate, and inner child sector this week, asking you to get more disciplined about what brings you joy. Over the next four and a half months, a passion project, dating pattern, creative goal, or dream you once felt excited about may return for revision. You may also notice where fear of failure, rejection, or looking foolish has kept you from fully expressing yourself. Give your creativity structure, make time for play, and stop treating joy like something you can squeeze in after every responsibility is handled.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your communication, learning, writing, and local community sector, making your voice a major part of your destiny timeline. Teaching, speaking, content creation, media, short trips, or learning a new skill could open important doors, especially when you’re willing to experiment with how you share your ideas. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your expansion sector, helping you release outdated beliefs, the need to always have the answer, or the pressure to chase the next big adventure before fully absorbing what the last one taught you.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your communication sector and brings something full circle from the February 17th solar eclipse. A conversation, writing project, announcement, course, contract, or idea may reach a turning point, or you may finally see how much your mindset has changed over the past six months. The message is ready to move now, Sag. Say it clearly, send it, publish it, and let the next chapter respond.

Capricorn Sun & Rising:

Capricorn, your ruler Saturn begins its retrograde in your home, family, and roots sector this week, asking you to take a closer look at the foundation beneath everything else you’re building. Over the next four and a half months, unfinished responsibilities at home, family dynamics, housing plans, or emotional patterns from childhood may need more of your attention. You may feel called to reorganize your space, set firmer boundaries with relatives, or finally deal with something you’ve been carrying privately for too long. The goal is to create more structure and security in your personal life so you’re not trying to build your future on top of emotional clutter.

The North Node enters Aquarius and begins an eighteen-month journey through your money, self-worth, and values sector, making financial independence and a stronger sense of personal value central to your destiny timeline. New income streams, unconventional business ideas, technology, or a different relationship with money could open important doors. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your intimacy and shared-resources sector, helping you release unhealthy financial entanglements, power struggles, debt patterns, or bonds that require too much of you emotionally.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your money sector and brings something full circle from the February 17th solar eclipse. A financial goal, income opportunity, pricing decision, or realization about your worth may reach a turning point now. The past six months have been showing you where you’re ready to stop settling, and this Full Moon gives you a much clearer sense of what you can build when you fully back yourself.

Aquarius Sun & Rising:

Aquarius, your ruler Saturn begins its retrograde in your communication, learning, and local community sector this week, asking you to become more intentional about the way you think, speak, and follow through. Over the next four and a half months, unfinished writing projects, delayed conversations, paperwork, courses, or commitments may come back around for your attention. You may also notice where scattered thinking, over-explaining, or speaking before you’ve fully processed something has created extra work for you. Slow down, organize your ideas, and give your voice enough structure to carry the weight of what you’re trying to build.

The North Node enters your sign this week, beginning one of the most personally significant eighteen-month chapters you’ve experienced in years. Your identity, appearance, confidence, independence, and sense of direction are all evolving, and life may begin pushing you toward choices that feel more authentic, even when they surprise the people around you. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your partnership sector, helping you release relationships, compromises, and people-pleasing patterns that have required you to shrink yourself or perform a version of who others expected you to be.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon takes place in your sign, illuminating how much you’ve changed since the February 17th solar eclipse. A personal goal, reinvention, decision, or new beginning may reach a major turning point, and you could suddenly see your next chapter with much more clarity. The Fire Horse has been carrying you toward this moment for six months, Aquarius, and now you’re being asked to stop looking behind you and fully step into the person you’ve become.

Pisces Sun & Rising:

Pisces, Saturn retrograde begins in your money, self-worth, and values sector this week, asking you to get more honest about how you earn, spend, save, and value your time. Over the next four and a half months, financial responsibilities you’ve postponed may need to be handled, and certain income goals may require more structure than inspiration alone. This is also a deeper lesson in self-worth, especially if you’ve been undercharging, over-giving, or letting fear make decisions for you. Create a realistic plan, tighten what needs tightening, and remember that consistency can be its own form of abundance.

The North Node enters Aquarius on the 26th and begins an eighteen-month journey through your spirituality, healing, and solitude sector, making your inner life a major part of your destiny timeline. Your intuition may become louder, your dreams more revealing, and your need for rest, privacy, or spiritual practice much harder to ignore. Meanwhile, the South Node in Leo moves through your health, work, and routine sector, helping you release perfectionism, overwork, and the habit of proving your value through constant productivity. Your body is going to have opinions about your schedule, so listen before it starts sending calendar invites.

Then, on July 29th, the Aquarius Full Moon illuminates your subconscious and brings something full circle from the February 17th solar eclipse. A hidden fear, emotional pattern, spiritual message, or chapter you’ve quietly been processing may finally become clear. The past six months have been preparing you to release something you no longer need to carry, and this Full Moon gives you the awareness to close that door with peace and enter August feeling lighter.

title: Angel Reese’s New Barbie Isn’t Just A Doll—It’s A Blueprint For Taking Up Space
text:
Angel Reese’s New Barbie Isn’t Just A Doll—It’s A Blueprint For Taking Up Space

In our eyes, Angel Reese was already a doll, but now she’s officially part of the Barbie family with her very own Barbie Signature doll created in her likeness, Reebok sneakers included. For Reese, the collaboration with Mattel represents a full-circle moment that extends well beyond her achievements on the hardwood.

“This moment is about so much more than my career on the court and represents the impact I hope to make beyond the game,” Reese tells Refinery29. “It’s about increasing representation for athletes while showing the next generation that they can be, and do, anything. I’ve always been driven to use my platform to create opportunities and inspire others, and I’m so excited to join Barbie in sharing my story and empowering girls to dream big.”

When the brand first reached out to partner with her, Reese says the reaction was immediate joy: “Honestly, it was a surreal moment, and I couldn’t stop smiling. I grew up loving Barbie, so getting the chance to work with the brand to create a doll of my own was a dream come true,” she shares. “I was excited because I knew this was an opportunity to bring together my passions, both on and off the court, by creating something that would help empower girls and celebrate the growing influence of women in sports.”

The Barbie design team worked closely with Reese to ensure the doll authentically reflected Reese’s signature style, from her court look down to her footwear.

“I was just blown away by how much it truly felt like me. The Barbie design team didn’t miss a single detail throughout the design process,” Reese says. “They captured my signature court look, from the custom #5 and #10 on my jersey to my signature single legging, right down to the Barbie-pink Reebok Angel Reese 1 Basketball Shoes. Seeing it all come together was a powerful reminder of my journey and how every step has been worth it. It’s one thing to see your likeness, but it’s another to feel like the doll truly captures your ethos, too.”

When asked to define what a Barbie means to her today, Reese emphasizes self-expression and confidence: “A Barbie is somebody who is confident, authentic, and not afraid to take up space. She knows who she is, goes after what she wants, and doesn’t let anybody define her. That’s the kind of woman I’ve always strived to be, and it’s why having my own Barbie means so much.”

Her ultimate hope is that young girls seeing the doll feel inspired to embrace every side of themselves without hesitation or compromise. “When a little girl sees this doll, I hope she can see herself,” Reese explains. “I want her to feel like she belongs in every room, on every court, and in every conversation. She never has to shrink herself to be successful. This doll, with her very own Barbie-pink Reebok Angel Reese 1 Basketball Shoes, is a reminder that you can be fierce, you can be stylish, and you can be a leader, all at the same time.”

Reese’s message for anyone chasing big ambitions is simple. Refuse to let perceived limits dictate your path. “My advice is to never let anyone else define what’s possible for you,” says Reese. “Stay true to yourself, embrace what makes you unique, and don’t be afraid to be a trailblazer. You don’t have to pick just one dream; you can chase them all. Keep dreaming big, working hard, staying true to who you are, and never be afraid to take up space.”

title: Paige DeSorbo On Dating Icks & Why It’s Never OK To Use AI To Flirt
text:
Paige DeSorbo On Dating Icks & Why It’s Never OK To Use AI To Flirt

We can all agree that dating is tough these days, and if you are like us, you wish you had someone to call when you simply cannot take it anymore. This is where former Summer House star, podcaster, and fashion designer Paige DeSorbo  and Bumble come in. They have teamed up to bring us Bee Line, a new social-first series where trusted voices answer real dating questions from Gen Z and Millennial daters. As one of the series hosts, Desorbo is ready to chime in with wisdom to keep us on track and looking for love. We caught up with DeSorbo to talk about dating do’s and don’ts and why dating apps aren’t so scary. 

Refinery29: In your Bee Line episode, you answered a question about using AI to create a dating profile. What are your thoughts on using ChatGPT to write your texts once you’ve matched with somebody? Is it a dating hack or an ick?

PD: That is so scary and terrifying. I saw a thing the other day that was like, “Kids will never know that we wrote an entire 10-page paper at 1:00 AM without having read the book,” which I just feel like builds character. If you can’t think of your own text messages. And calling your friend is much different than asking a robot. If you’re asking a robot, I need you to seek therapy. I think that’s crazy. I don’t like it. 

Apparently, it’s a trend.

PD: I don’t like that because how do you know someone’s humor? You know? And then when you get in real life, you can’t ask the computer! So no, I don’t like that at all. [laughs]

My boss was extremely confused about the idea of a FaceTime date. She was like, “This is what people are doing?” So, a FaceTime date before an actual first date. Is that a good idea or a bad idea?

PD: I kind of love that. I love a cold call. I love that we met, we know we’re going out, we have the date set, but you cold called me randomly, and if it’s FaceTime, I like that. I feel like some of the best dates I’ve gone out on, I’ve FaceTimed before. So. I’m a fan.

What do you think are the components for a good FaceTime date?

PD: I think come as you are. Whatever time of night or day that you set up the FaceTime, I think what you would normally be wearing. Say you’re doing it at 5:00, and you’re in a workout outfit, that’s really cute. If you’re doing it at 8:00 and you’re in pajamas, adorable. That feels more authentic to me. Whatever you would’ve been doing at that time, I feel like that’s how you show up.

Bumble says people are dating more intentionally now. Do you think people actually know what they want if they’re dating intentionally, or are they just getting better at knowing what they don’t want?

PD: I think probably a combination of both. I feel like dating in general is gathering information and deciding what you like and what you don’t like. To know what you like, you also have to know what you dislike. I do think that people are dating more intentionally now, specifically women. But I feel like women have always dated intentionally.

What does it mean to be exclusive?

PD: Look, I’m 33, so I look at things differently now, obviously, than when I was in my 20s. When I was in my 20s, did someone at some point say, “Hey, we’re exclusive, but we’re not dating.” And I was like, “I love it,” like amazing? Absolutely. I do think that’s what your 20s are for, to make these mistakes. I feel like sometimes Gen Z’s a little nervous to make mistakes. Now at 33, if someone told me we were exclusive, I would be like, “I don’t know what that means.” We’re either together, or we’re not. But if I’m 22 years old, I think it is sort of a rite of passage to have a situationship. It helps you figure out what you like and what you don’t like. But after a certain age, you have to set boundaries. No one’s telling me we’re exclusive at 33. That would be insane.

Are dating apps making us pickier or helping us stop wasting time?

PD: I think dating apps definitely help you stop wasting time because you can get to the nitty-gritty immediately. If I see someone on a dating profile and all their pictures are outdoors, we’re probably not going to be the best match. I’d like to know now rather than wasting your time and mine. And no one’s setting us up in real life if you just came back from a hike, ’cause my friends know that I’m not partaking.

So best advice for getting back into dating after you’ve been in a long relationship. I feel like the apps can be scary sometimes to go back on there.

PD: I feel like the apps are only as scary as you make them. You can’t put all your energy into one specific thing. I think going on the apps is a great way to ease into it, because you’re still in the comfort of your bed, and nothing bad can happen when you’re in your bed. I don’t feel like they’re as scary as some people say. My best remedy will always and forever be having a girls’ night out. Any time I’ve become single, the first thing I’ve done is go out with my girlfriends, ’cause it reminds you how much fun it is to be socializing. Going out with a guy first, it’s a lot of pressure. I think going on dating apps, even if you don’t go on any of the dates, is a good way to ease into it.

If you go on the first date, do you think chemistry needs to be instant, or can it build if there’s no fireworks on date one?

PD: I’m not a builder. I don’t have time. I don’t have time for you to maybe think I’m amazing. In the first 10 seconds or nothing. I’ve never been a slow-burn person. I’m pretty all in. I’m very decisive, and so if someone’s not decisive, that’s a turn-off for me. Be obsessed with me or die.

I’m going to need to write that one down. Be obsessed with me or die.

PD: Get away!

Let’s end on a quick rapid fire game: ick or no ick? They wear a baseball hat to your first date.

PD: Ick, no. This isn’t a baseball game.

They try to hold your hand.

PD: Not an ick. I think affection is nice.

Says “females” instead of “women.”

PD: Ick. Unless you’re talking about a doctor or a medical situation, do not say female to me.

The first date was longer than three hours.

PD: Not an ick, because that means you’re having a good time.

Asking what your attachment style is.

PD: Unless they’re a therapist, not an ick. But that’s very situational. If some random guy was just like, “What’s your attachment style?” I don’t know if I would love it, but also if we were having a conversation about it, maybe that would be nice. Enlighten me a little. What do you think it is?

Orders a martini in a rocks glass because martini glasses are too feminine

PD: Okay, if he said that they’re too feminine, that would be an ick, but initially not an ick because I’ve done that as well because I spill it all the time. I think it’s easier to hold and drink in a regular glass. So that’s not an ick for me.

They are holding a fish in their dating profile picture.

PD: Not an ick; we’re just not compatible.

If they send you a five-minute voice note.

PD: No, I like that. It shows he has a personality, and he can put a sentence together for five minutes. We’ll take it where we can get it.

The classic one: they message you every day but won’t make plans.

PD: Ick. Yeah. I don’t need a pen pal.

No pen pals 2026, that’s my motto.

title: No Clock-Ins, No Micromanaging, & 100-Year Sweaters: Inside Brunello Cucinelli’s Anti-Corporate Fashion House
text:
No Clock-Ins, No Micromanaging, & 100-Year Sweaters: Inside Brunello Cucinelli’s Anti-Corporate Fashion House

Let’s be honest: when most of us hear “Italian luxury knitwear titan,” our brains don’t immediately leap to labor rights, workplace dignity, or radical empathy. We think of four-figure price tags and pristine neutral palettes that live strictly in the closets of the top 1%.

So while watching the new documentary on Brunello Cucinelli (Brunello: The Gracious Visionary), I wasn’t necessarily expecting a masterclass on how to treat human beings with basic dignity. But that is precisely what makes Cucinelli’s story so fascinating, and why it feels like such an antidote to the fast pace of the fashion industry.

At the core of this film is a concept Cucinelli calls “Humanistic Capitalism.” It sounds like a lofty corporate buzzword until you actually look at how his house operates. In an industry where burnout is often treated like a badge of honor and modern hustle culture demands we grind ourselves into dust, Cucinelli has spent decades proving a radically simple point: You can build a billion-dollar empire without exploiting the people who build it for you.

Before he was the “King of Cashmere,” Cucinelli was just a scrappy young guy trying to break into the market. Founded in the late 1970s and scaling through the ’80s, the brand’s origins carry an ambitious charm. In the early days, he would literally change his voice on phone calls, pretending to be different secretaries and executives to create the illusion that he was running a massive, established enterprise.

As a great philosopher once said, “Delulu is the solulu,” because it worked. During his first showcase, he managed to sell over 11,000 sweaters—in just two days. Manufacturing early demand through sheer audacity paid off and led to him making a legendary American debut at Barneys New York (RIP to the iconic fashion mecca).

Staying true to his values, Cucinelli would tell investors “If you’re after a business that profits at the expense of humanity, this is not the company you should invest in.”

When he launched his brand in 1978, fashion moved at a completely different pace. Fast-fashion, micro-trends, weekly drops, and viral $10 internet hauls weren’t even on the horizon. Garments were bought with care, repaired when worn, and expected to hold their ground over time. But still, Cucinelli wanted to push that ethos to the extreme, asking his mother to help him create a sweater designed to last 100 years.

In an era saturated with cheap, disposable clothing that pills after two washes, the concept of a 100-year garment isn’t just about high-end craftsmanship. It’s an act of anti-capitalist resistance against consumerism. It asks us to re-evaluate our entire relationship with what we buy.

As a Shopping Director, a huge part of my daily life is centered on vetting trends, testing products, and telling you what’s actually worth putting in your cart. But lately, my personal editorial ethos has shifted from simply asking, “What else do we need to buy?” to “How can we buy better, not more?”

It’s an idea that actress Liu Tao echoes in the documentary when reflecting on why Brunello Cucinelli resonates so deeply: “This brand flatters my body’s proportions and gives me confidence. That’s why I love this brand.” True luxury isn’t about hiding your body or constantly chasing the next trend. It’s about proportions, self-worth, and clothes that give back to the wearer for a lifetime.

Where the film truly shifts from a standard fashion profile into a blueprint for corporate reform is inside the company’s factory walls in Solomeo, Italy.

At Cucinelli’s headquarters, workers are given keys to the facilities. There are no rigid clock-ins or draconian micromanagement, just a fundamental trust in the people who craft the product. Beyond that, roughly 20% of company profits are directly funneled back into “beautifying humanity,” from renovating the medieval village of Solomeo to maintaining public parks and community spaces.

The defining moment of this philosophy took place in March 2020. I’m sure we all remember where we were during that time. As global markets froze and uncertainty swept through the entire world, Cucinelli hosted a call with his entire workforce (around 9,000 people across the brand’s ecosystem). His message wasn’t about cutting costs or thinning out payroll. Instead, he made a firm, explicit commitment: For the next two years, he promised zero layoffs, guaranteed full salaries, and pledged that the company would not ask its suppliers for discounts. That’s enough to make anyone ask, “Where do I sign up?” In an era where tech giants and media houses routinely announce mass layoffs via automated emails, Cucinelli’s decision was a stark reminder that executive leadership is, at its core, a moral choice.

The documentary closes with two quiet, visually stunning scenes that are still etched in my mind. The first is an impossibly long family dinner table stretched across an open field in Italy. But the people sitting around it aren’t just Cucinelli’s immediate relatives. It’s his extended work family. A literal visual representation of what happens when a business shares its prosperity instead of hoarding it at the top.

The final image returns to a recurring motif throughout the film: Cucinelli playing cards. As a young man, he spent hours in local Italian bars cutting decks. Throughout the documentary, we see him at the table, but the final scene reveals who sits across from him. He isn’t playing against a rival designer or a corporate competitor. He’s playing against his younger self. It’s a striking metaphor for how Cucinelli operates. From a young boy guiding cows through Umbrian fields—obsessing over making sure the plow lines were perfectly straight—to building one of the most respected fashion houses in history, his focus has never been on beating the competition. It’s always been about self-mastery, controlling what you can control, and striving to be a better version of yourself than you were yesterday. That’s the ultimate main-character energy flex.

title: What Is “Skin Preservation,” & Why Is It Everywhere Right Now?
text:
What Is “Skin Preservation,” & Why Is It Everywhere Right Now?

So often in the beauty space, trends are little more than repackaged ideas from decades past. The term anti-aging, for example, has been rightly scrutinized for years, gradually giving way to a new buzzword that’s popping up not only in the healthcare space, but in beauty, as well: longevity. 

Where anti-aging positions wrinkles, dullness, and other visible signs of time as problems to fear and fix, skin longevity — and now, its close cousin, skin preservation, which I’ll get to shortly — is rooted in maintaining healthy skin for the long haul. Rather than chasing quick fixes or making you feel guilty about your choices, the goal is to support your skin with consistent habits and ingredients that help it look its best for as long as possible. (We’ve already seen this shift in products like Tatcha’s The Longevity Memory Cream, a firm R29 favorite, and Paula’s Choice CellularYouth Longevity Serum, both of which lean into the idea of protecting skin’s future rather than reversing its past.)

Most recently, there’s No7’s new Prime Forever collection: a four-piece skincare routine built around the concept of preserving skin before visible aging really begins to accelerate.  

DashDividers_1_500x100

What is “skin preservation,” & how does it differ from “anti-aging”? 

Skin longevity and skin preservation are essentially two sides of the same coin: helping your skin look and function at its best for as long as possible. What I was more interested in, however, was how that concept differs from the traditional idea of anti-aging as it’s been marketed for decades. 

Multiple factors contribute to accelerated skin aging. Free radicals create oxidative stress that damages skin cells, UVA and UVB rays break down collagen and cause pigmentation, and naturally occurring enzymes gradually degrade collagen and elastin, leading to loss of firmness over time. “Skin preservation is less about the quick fix, whereas even a few years ago it was more about, ‘I want immediate gratification. I want to see instant results,'” says New York-based dermatologist Dr. Marisa Garshick. “In general, people are taking a much more proactive approach with their health, and I think we’re definitely seeing that with skin, too.” In other words, instead of waiting until concerns appear, there’s a new focus toward building a routine that helps slow down visible changes before they happen — a subtle but fascinating shift in how we think about (and talk about) skin. 

All of that brings me to No7, where I recently got an early look at the Prime Forever range. Prime Forever is somewhat niche in that it’s uniquely suited to people around my age, when the earliest signs of aging are beginning to emerge. At 32, I have very few fine lines or wrinkles, and still benefit from the naturally bouncy, collagen-rich skin of my twenties. I credit that largely to good genetics, a daily sunscreen habit, and staying out of the sun whenever possible — but everyone’s skin ages eventually, and I’m more interested in keeping mine as resilient and radiant as possible. 

That proactive, ounce-of-prevention approach isn’t unique to me — far from it. “Most people don’t want to dramatically change what they look like,” Dr. Garshick tells me. “They just want to keep looking and feeling good.” And that’s exactly where skin preservation fits in: maintaining what you have rather than trying to undo years of accumulated damage later. 

Keep reading for my review of each No7 Prime Forever product and why they deserve a spot in your skincare regimen.  

DashDividers_1_500x100

Prime Forever Transformative Gel-Oil-Milk Cleanser, $19.99

The four-step routine begins with the Prime Forever Transformative Gel-Oil-Milk Cleanser, which dispenses as a gel before emulsifying into a silky, milky texture with water. Packed with glycerin to help draw moisture into the skin, plus antioxidant-rich vitamin E, it left my face feeling clean without that tight, stripped feeling. The texture is absolutely divine, and I find it works best as a luxurious morning cleanse or as the second step after an oil cleanser in the evening.

Prime Forever Preservation Serum, $39.99

Next comes the Prime Forever Preservation Serum, a lightweight formula that tackles multiple concerns at once. Alongside hydrating hyaluronic acid, it features niacinamide to help brighten and support the skin barrier, plus peptides that work to boost collagen and elastin over time. Despite packing in so many actives, it didn’t irritate my sensitive, breakout-prone skin one bit. (Also, the texture is incredibly silky and absorbed almost instantly; my skin practically drank it up.) It layers beautifully under moisturizer, never feeling sticky or pilling, making it an easy addition to both morning and nighttime routines.

Prime Forever Weightless Moisturizer, $39.99

An unexpected standout from the collection was the Prime Forever Weightless Moisturizer. Despite its cushiony gel texture, it delivers the kind of lasting hydration I’d normally expect from a much richer cream. Alongside hydrating humectants like glycerin and sodium hyaluronate, and the range’s signature peptide-and-antioxidant complex, it leaves skin looking plump and feeling comfortably moisturized without crossing into greasy territory. This is true for the entire Prime Forever lineup, but the textures really impressed me; if I were testing these blind, I’d assume they came from a luxury beauty counter rather than the drugstore aisle. 

Prime Forever SPF50 Primer, $34.99

Last but certainly not least is the Prime Forever SPF 50 Primer, which serves as the final step in your morning skincare routine. While it’s designed to prep skin for makeup, I’d happily wear it on its own thanks to its smoothing finish and broad-spectrum sun protection. Formulated with vitamin E and soothing aloe vera, it helps keep skin comfortable throughout the day while chemical UV filters provide completely transparent SPF 50 protection without even a whisper of white cast. What impressed me most, though, was the finish: it softens the look of texture, keeps excess shine at bay, and leaves my skin looking naturally radiant rather than starkly matte. SPF-infused primers are somewhat of a growing category, and I’m generally in favor of anything that makes UV protection feel more effortless. Still, think of this as a bonus rather than replacing your primary sunscreen to ensure you’re getting adequate UV protection.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Final Thoughts

\In a skincare landscape where expensive products and even more expensive in-office treatments like neuromodulators, fillers, and lasers claim to turn back the clock, I was honestly impressed at No7’s Prime Forever range. The formulas feel luxurious to use, but the prices remain relatively accessible, ranging from $20 to $39. And as gratifying as it is to see fast results, testing this routine is something that will inevitably require patience on my end; given where my skin is currently at, it’s likely that I won’t be able to truly appreciate the results of practicing safe sun and having a good skincare routine until five, maybe even 10, years from now. But you know what they say about marathons and sprints.

title: Saturn Retrograde In Aries Is Here — & You’ll Need To Set Some Boundaries
text:
Saturn Retrograde In Aries Is Here — & You’ll Need To Set Some Boundaries

Mark your calendars because as of July 26th, another planet will shift into its retrograde orbit: Saturn in Aries. From July 26th to December 10th, Saturn will make a cosmic U-turn, forcing us to face our fears. Michelle Tea, spiritualist and author of several books, says “Saturn retrograde can be a real ass-kicking for relationships, but necessary.” The author of upcoming book, Free Love: Adventures in Marriage and Polyamory, continues, “If things have been sliding, neglected, ignored, Saturn gives you another chance to do right. Saturn is not merciless — Saturn roots for us! — but Saturn warns us as well to not waste but we’ve been given, including a second chance!” 

Don’t be too disheartened though as Saturn retrograde isn’t necessarily a bad time for us to plan for the future. When the austere planet begins to moonwalk, it offers a moment of reflection in which we can plot our next moves, so get ready. It’s imperative we know how to temper the energy and pursue our goals without being too pushy. Saturn retrograde offers us the chance to create a game plan that fits our daily demands, lifestyle, and schedule. We aren’t try-hards; on the contrary, we’re able to attain our goals without stressing over the outcome. The path to success may not look like what we thought it would, but it takes us to where we need to be.

This retrograde is a moment in time when we will boss up in all our endeavors. Saturn’s backspin offers us the chance to take charge and to elevate our businesses to the next level. When direct, Saturn represents company management or the principal imposing rules in school; the opposite is true when retrograde. Saturn’s regressive state evolves into something more, giving us the wherewithal to implement new visions and heightening our desire to innovate, allowing us to impose radical values on societal norms and standards. We aren’t afraid to take a stand.

Setting healthy aspirations can be challenging because we are assessing our circumstances intuitively. Rigidity is not on the agenda, which is why adhering to a schedule is useless. Life as we know it is in flux, so go with the flow. Use the retrograde to revise programs, routines, or habits. But do not try to change everything all at once, because it won’t go over so well and will be difficult to stick to once the retrograde completes its cycle. We need to do research and refine our situation before getting on board with a new program to ensure it aligns with our long-term goals.

Despite all the retrograde madness occurring at the moment from Mercury, Neptune, and Pluto (in September, Uranus starts diving backward), Saturn’s backsplash urges us to level up our relationships. As a result, we may be more inclined to connect with others intimately. Pursuing a relationship could be concerning if we do not choose to yield our passions. The caveat is that jumping in too soon before getting to know the other person can create problems if we aren’t careful, so make the effort to get to know them and take it slow. Intentional dating is advisable to ensure our needs and wants are satisfied.

The key ingredients for a successful Saturn retrograde are implementing boundaries — not only for others but for ourselves as well. We should stay in our lane and not swerve into criticizing others or casting judgment until we know the full story. We expect the same from others, so we must practice what we preach.

title: Go Off, Sis: Jenee Naylor of HighLowLuxxe on Making a Plan and Letting Go of Perfection
text:
Go Off, Sis: Jenee Naylor of HighLowLuxxe on Making a Plan and Letting Go of Perfection

For Jenee Naylor, success requires a roadmap. Now, that doesn’t mean following a traditional path or climbing the corporate ladder, but rather looking to others for what is possible. ‘Seeing is believing,’ the founder of 12PM Studios tells host Erica Chidi Cohen, and now she hopes to inspire other Black women by sharing all that she’s learned. 

Before Jenee made her first major splash with her blog HighLowLuxxe, she got her start on the floor of a Target store in the DMV. She started managing a team of people and moving up the ranks. “I learned how to be a business person through that role,” she shares. She thrived in leadership, particularly because it allowed her to pour into others; she loved teaching, training, and getting people promoted; she was a campus recruiter for Howard. In many ways, it laid the foundation for what was to come. Working for a big store taught her the value of strategy and everything having a place.  “So much of my personality is about being efficient and making the most of things.” 

Her blog, HighLowLuxxe, was “something clever that represented me,” Jenee says it was true to who she was at the time, mostly shopping fast fashion but splurging on something with her bonus check. It was the perfect blend of Jenee’s expertise and her sharing what she was learning about the world of luxury. Part of what made the blog such a success was Jenee’s honest approach to creating content. Sure, she’d have a flawless beat, but she’d shoot her videos in one take. And authenticity might be the key to her long-term success. “Consistency and longevity are hard to maintain if you are putting on an act,” she shares. 

It takes a lot of bravery to walk away from something when it’s working, and working well. Although HighLowLuxxe was a resounding success, Jenee felt called to build something in her own name. She

walked away from high/low luxe to build 12PM Studios, her extremely chic sunglasses company. Why eyewear? For one, it’s “the only thing I care enough about to talk about every day,” Jenee laughs. But also, once Jenee reached the point of success where others were photographing her, she realized sunglasses can offer a bit of protection, a very chic shield from the outside world. So, she looked at what was out there, how others were succeeding, trusted her instincts, and built herself another roadmap. Learn more about how she got from managing a Target to selling her products in Target in this episode of Go Off, Sis.

title: It’s The Summer Of Chunky Jewelry Maxxing
text:
It’s The Summer Of Chunky Jewelry Maxxing

This summer’s biggest trend, quite literally, is chunky jewelry. Unlike most seasonal trends, this one is not going anywhere anytime soon. Once you fall for chunky jewelry, it quietly becomes part of your personal style, to the point where people can’t imagine you without it.

No one embraced the spirit of chunky jewelry quite like the late, great fashion icon Iris Apfel. Long before oversized bangles and sculptural necklaces took over the fashion world, she built an unforgettable personal style around maximalist jewelry. Her bold accessories became a reflection of her fearless personality, making it almost impossible to picture her without them. And from what we’re seeing now, maybe we’re all channeling our inner Iris Apfel this summer.

Whether it’s a beach day, a city stroll, dinner plans, or a night out, chunky jewelry belongs everywhere. After all, an accessory is the finishing touch that can completely transform any outfit.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bella 🦋 (@bellahadid)

Although the chunky jewelry trend can be traced back to the 2010s, fashion has been moving in this direction again over the past few years. Schiaparelli was among the first to bring statement jewelry back into the spotlight in 2023 with its surrealist accessories. And as maximalism gradually made its way from the runway into everyday wardrobes, surrealist jewelry evolved into something far more wearable.

This change became even more visible on the latest runways, with Sarah Burton’s debut Givenchy SS26 collection showcasing oversized necklaces and statement earrings, while Zimmermann’s SS26 collection featured sculptural jewelry alongside its romantic summer aesthetic.

This summer, the bigger the better. Less layering of dainty pieces, and more styling with larger accessories. Sometimes, all it takes is one great find to become the centerpiece of your wardrobe. My go-to summer outfit formula starts with a white tank top, relaxed linen trousers, oversized sunglasses, kitten heel mules, and as much chunky jewelry as I can get. Colorful resin bangles, sculptural earrings, and playful shapes always work together. The only rule I stick to is keeping each jewelry category consistent: silver with silver, resin with resin. Another key element is to let just one jewelry category do the talking.

During the day, style a sheer cape top with denim shorts, flip-flops, and oversized resin bangles for an effortless summer look. For evenings, pair a simple midi summer dress with sculptural gold earrings, chunky gold rings, and strappy heels. For me, everything else in your outfit can change, but a great chunky ring stack can remain your signature finishing touch. The trick is this: chunky rings are the ultimate day-to-night jewelry, and, sometimes, even piece you’ll wear for a lifetime, like Dua Lipa’s chunky engagement ring, which has quickly become one of the most talked-about jewelry pieces of the year.

In the summer, chunky jewelry can take the form of an abstract shape, like fruit, flowers, or seashells. Pair oversized shell earrings with a monochrome matching set for an effortless vacation look, or let a stack of colorful resin bangles elevate a simple white sundress. One of my personal favorites in my jewelry drawer is a pair of oversized cherry earrings, which I happily wear with everything from a white tank and denim shorts to a simple midi dress. Whichever way you choose to style it, chunky jewelry is the perfect trend to express yourself and be as loud as you want, like Apfel proudly did. 

And when fall arrives, Valentino’s FW26 collection proves that oversized jewelry also works just as well layered over knitwear and tailored coats. You can also layer thick bracelets over fitted long-sleeve tops and style oversized chokers over turtlenecks. Voilà, you’re ready to take this “summer” trend into the cooler months.

title: Nicolandria Is (Reportedly) Over. Why Do We Care So Much About Celebrity Breakups?
text:
Nicolandria Is (Reportedly) Over. Why Do We Care So Much About Celebrity Breakups?

Love is dead. Or so it feels for many fans after celebrity couples announce their breakups. Love Island Season 7 stars Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe have broken up after a year of dating, PEOPLE exclusively reports. The popular couple “decided to part ways” as, the PEOPLE source claims, “the distance between them and their busy schedules made it challenging to maintain their connection.” The source continues: “They still remain close friends. They share a deep love and respect for each other and will always support one another whenever possible.”

2026 has also ushered in other high profile celebrity breakups, like Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff (a Qualley source told PEOPLE that the couple is “figuring things out” amid the split), Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater (she has since reconnected with her ex, Ricky Alvarez), Sue Bird and Megan Rapinoe (lesbians around the world were devastated) and Megan Thee Stallion and Klay Thompson, just to name a few. Each of these breakups made headlines (for various reasons) and caused our timelines to speculate, rage, mourn, or all three. It’s natural to be upset when a couple you think you know — or one you were simply rooting hard for — breaks up. When it comes to Nic and Olandria, they have a very specific microscope on their relationship, and the amount of parasocial obsession with their love story seemed to reach heights the internet had never seen. There are the “contract is up!” people who think they were never really dating in the first place, the “love is dead!” camp who pinned all their romantic hopes on the duo, and the “I don’t believe it” folks who are living in denial that PEOPLE magazine is a celeb-friendly source often used by publicists as an unofficial “official” way to get news to the public. It’s safe to say that Nicolandria is done. What’s clear for sure is that everyone has an opinion, and people really care about celebrity breakups.

In 2023, after the breakup of Joe Manganiello and Sofia Vergara, Alicia Vrajlal wrote for Refinery29 that, “Admittedly, I’m one of [the people who mourn celeb breakups]. Like many fans, I was devastated when I heard the news and overwhelmed with a sense of sorrow and disbelief. It can’t be true. Everything seemed to be going so well. I almost wanted to cry. “

But in a world where Hollywood splits are so common, and celebrity worship is becoming at once more intense than ever and more scrutinized, why do we care so much about the relationship breakdowns of famous people we’ve never met?

‘Relationship goals’ is a term often thrown around when it comes to celebrities, because they tend to publicly portray the ideal or fantasy of what a relationship looks like or can aspire to be. But our understanding of #RelationshipGoals has shifted. In 2021, we wrote that, “Not only do #RelationshipGoals fetishize an image that’s curated and not real, they also glorify a type of love that prioritizes staying together (aka building a brand) over anything else.” When we look at stars and project them to be attractive yet down-to-earth, and have busy careers but still find time for dates and cute grocery trips together, we are inadvertently creating the idea that their romance can survive the odds, no matter what. In reality, everything ends, and we don’t know these people. That said, it’s natural to be curious and to care.

“Many of us are interested in celebrities and other public figures and are naturally curious about their lives,” psychologist Dr Marny Lishman tells Refinery29. “At some level, their lives are so unattainable and almost fantasy-like to us, but at another level, many of the same trials and tribulations they endure are not unlike our own.”

It’s because of this that we live vicariously through them when we’re single, and unconsciously strive for the relationship success they have when we’re in a relationship of our own. With that being said, it only makes sense that when a celebrity couple calls it quits, we too feel a sudden loss. We are worried about the Nicolandria hive.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ericka Hart, M.Ed. (@ihartericka)

In 2023, Nina, 23, said she felt this loss when Lisa Bonet and Jason Momoa broke up in January 2022. At the time, when Phoebe Bridgers and Paul Mescal (who is now dating Gracie Abrams) called time on their romance, Nina was also shook.

“While I definitely don’t get upset about all the famous breakups, these ones truly made me sad,” she tells Refinery29, explaining she was inspired by certain aspects of each couple’s relationships.

“When couples you look up to split up, it kind of gives you a ‘romance and love are dead’ feeling, which sucks. They gave the impression that even relationships with barriers — age differences, dealing with so much fame and gossip or personal drama — stood a chance.”

Lishman explains that we’re often only exposed to one version of reality when it comes to celebrity relationships. This makes our disbelief that much stronger when the romances collapse.

“We idolize their relationships too as we idolize the celebrity, so when the ‘seemingly perfect’ relationship ends, we grieve for the ending of what we perceived as perfection,” says Lishman.

“We see a fairly edited version of reality, so it’s hard to understand why a seemingly perfect relationship would end. At times we are shocked because it ‘looked’ so good.”

Nina agrees, saying that she has “put celebrity couples on a pedestal” in the past, looking to them for “inspiration and confirmation of romance in the world.” So when it all comes crumbling down, it’s a bit of a reality check.

“When they break up, it’s just a sad reminder that no one is immune to the realities and difficulties of love and commitment,” she says.

Lishman explains that this realization is very normal. While it’s hard for many of us to process the news when a seemingly perfect celeb couple breaks up, we know that to some degree (without the fame and fortune), they are just like us.

“They are complex, imperfect creatures that go through highs and lows in life, just like we do. They lose love, they break up, they grieve, they get rejected — just like the rest of us.”

Social media has only exacerbated our passionate responses to celebrity splits. In a time when we watch so many celebrities carefully curate their TikToks with ‘relatable’ couple vids, or flirt up a storm in the comments section, how can we not get deeply invested in their blossoming romances?

“Social media allows us to connect more with them [celebrities], and also be more informed about what’s going in their lives. It gives us more information than traditional media, so we seem to be more invested,” says Lishman.

We’re also seeing more celebrities who find love on a reality TV dating shows (like Nic and Olandria) or on the set of a film, which makes us feel like we’ve been on the journey with them — from the first date to the breakup announcement post on Instagram. And in some cases (like Love Island couples), we actually have. No matter how hard you felt it when High School Musical stars Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens split in 2010, we weren’t privy to watching their entire love story play out on camera. Sure, we watched the young love blossom from HSM 1 to 3, and it’s hard not to recall their affection and red carpet cuteness fondly, it’s a whole different beast when a couple’s first kiss and every flirtation is caught on camera. That’s why we’re in the depths of people being extremely not normal about celebrity breakups (just look at how some Swifties still talk about Joe Alwyn). For the celebs, navigating the public scrutiny also seems to be tougher than ever.

Olandria just had to clap back at unverified gossip platform, DeuxMoi, for circulating a rumor that she’s been hooking up with Travis Scott. Olandria denied this claim and commented, “I hope you have your lawyers ready bc I have mine.” According to Cosmo, Olandria’s comment has been deleted or hidden from the public. DeuxMoi confirmed in a pinned comment, “Update: Olandria denied(?) this rumor but blocked this account so her comment, which was pinned was not showing it was from her.”

As the likes of Nic, Olandria, and other celebs, continue to navigate their respective breakups, there will always be fans who are still rooting for them, who will shamelessly keep caring about their favorite celebrity couples (and their breakups), in the hope that there will be just as many moments filled with joy as there will be grief. Some of these people need to go outside and touch grass, while others (like us!) are invested in healthy, completely normal ways. (It’s a good thing Tom Holland and Zendaya are going to stay together forever, right? Right!?) These are people’s real lives, but often it can feel like we’re still watching a fictional love story play out, or that the stakes are just who’s coupled up in a villa. That’s why you see so many people unable to let go of their fave celeb couples — for better and for worse.

After all, how many of us have secretly harbored the hope that Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck will rekindle their flame one day (again!)? For some couples, a breakup is certainly the right decision. But as fans, it’s easy to hope that some of our favorite couples will get back together (again, think Bennifer 2.0, or Justin and Hailey Bieber or OTP Tom and Zendaya). Regardless of whether the split is temporary or permanent, we just need to remember that hope is not dead, and neither is love.
